pob.text: But Jonah rose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of Yahweh[a]. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. He paid its fare and went down into it to go with them to Tarshish[c][b], away from the presence of Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went aboard to sail for Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.

pob.text: But Yahweh hurled a great wind onto the sea[a], and there was a great storm on the sea[b], so that the ship seemed about to be broken up.

pob.text: Then the sailors were afraid[a], and each cried out to his god. They threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten it for themselves. But Yonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the vessel[b], and he lay down and fell fast asleep.

pob.text: So the captain came near to him and said to him[a], “What do you mean, sleeper? Get up, call on your god. Perhaps the god will give thought to us[c][b], so that we may not perish.”

spob.text: The captain came over to him and said, “How can you be sleeping? Get up and call on your god! Perhaps the god will take notice of us, so that we may not die.”

pob.text: And they said[a], each man to his companion, “Come, let us cast lots, so that we may know on whose account this evil has come upon us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

spob.text: They said to one another, “Come, let us cast lots to find out who is the reason this disaster[a] has come upon us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

pob.text: Then they said to him[a], “Please tell us on whose account this trouble has come upon us. What is your occupation, and where do you come from? What is your land[b], and from what people are you?”

pob.text: He said to them[a], “I am a Hebrew, and I fear Yahweh, the God of heaven[b], who made the sea and the dry land.”

pob.text: But the men rowed hard to return to the dry land[a], but they could not[c][b], because the sea kept growing more and more stormy against them.

pob.text: Then they cried out to Yahweh and said[a], “Please, Yahweh, do not let us perish on account of this man's life, and do not put innocent blood on us, for you, Yahweh[b], have done as you pleased.”
